title: File version history in a single DynamoDB table
name: File version store

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code models and queries file versions in the table? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Two clients both read HEAD as version 4 and call commitVersion at the same time. What happens?
choices: Both writes succeed and the later one overwrites version 5
One transaction succeeds; the other is cancelled because its conditions fail, and nothing from it is written
Both transactions fail because DynamoDB transactions cannot touch the same partition
The second client's version item is written but HEAD is not updated

questions.prompt: Why are version items and the HEAD item stored under the same partition key?
choices: So a single Query on pk can retrieve a file's whole history and HEAD can be read with a cheap GetItem on the same key
Because TransactWriteCommand requires all items to share a partition key
To spread writes for a busy file across many partitions
So that deleting HEAD automatically deletes all versions

questions.prompt: A file has never been committed. What does commitVersion do when called with expectedHead = 0?
choices: It fails because HEAD does not exist and version = :expected cannot be evaluated
It writes version 0 and a HEAD of 0
It writes VER#1 and creates HEAD with version 1, because attribute_not_exists(pk) passes for the missing HEAD
It writes VER#1 but skips HEAD since no previous HEAD existed
